brief.subject: Diesel falls 16.5 cents to $6.127; tighter peak tests shippers
brief.headline: Diesel slides 16.5 cents as a tighter peak squeezes old shipper bid playbooks
brief.dek: Diesel averages $6.127, rigid shipper contracts strain in a firmer market, intermodal sets a record and a Texas carrier faces federal charges.
brief.lede: The national diesel average dropped 16.5 cents to $6.127 per gallon, a welcome break on fuel costs, though oil markets remain volatile.

sections.heading: Diesel drops sharply this week
bullets: $6.127 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-09.
Down 16.5 cents (2.6%) from the prior week, easing per-mile fuel costs for small carriers.
Down 5.2 cents over four weeks, so most of the relief landed in just the last week.
Oil markets remain volatile on geopolitical and refining risks, so keep fuel surcharge terms in place.

sections.heading: Rigid shipper contracts strain at peak
bullets: Long rate locks, steep penalties and little flexibility have been some shippers' standard bid strategy from 2022 through 2025.
A brokerage leader at A. Duie Pyle says that approach is breaking down as the market tightens.
Shippers stuck with stale contract rates may lean on spot capacity, opening better-paying loads for small carriers.

sections.heading: Intermodal hits record in October
bullets: Intermodal set a record in October, according to the AAR.
Rail volumes rose across much of the freight economy, a sign of continued demand.
More intermodal means more drayage work near ramps but competition for some long-haul dry van lanes.

sections.heading: Texas owner indicted over 57 drivers
bullets: 57 unauthorized B-1 visa drivers were allegedly used by a Laredo trucking company owner to haul domestic freight.
The owner faces federal charges, showing enforcement against illegal domestic hauling is active.
Carriers playing by the rules lose loads to operators cutting corners, so this crackdown matters to rates.

sections.heading: Ocean trade: fees delayed, rates ease
bullets: Two more months: the U.S. postponed punitive fees on China-linked ships until January.
Transpacific ocean rates eased slightly as peak demand at U.S. ports slows.
Rates stay elevated year over year, so expect import drayage volumes to cool rather than collapse.
